notes: Round 2 addresses most prior findings: tests/test_resume.py now exists with 5 integration tests bringing total to 17 (>15), scripts/checkpoint_demo.py is created and its output captured, evidence includes checkpoint directory listing and pytest tail for both suites. However, two prior findings remain partially unaddressed: (1) the snapshot-before-expensive-call hook is mentioned in evidence text but has no test verifying it triggers, and (2) the integration test in test_resume.py simulates a checkpoint+resume rather than implementing the brief's exact MAX_STEPS_THIS_RUN fault-injection pattern with halted=True/reason assertions. Additionally, the live demo is a simulation that does not actually exercise resume_goal() end-to-end with a real LLM call replacement — it only verifies checkpoints survive a simulated kill, not that resume reconstructs and continues execution.
findings: Add a unit test in tests/test_checkpoint.py (or test_react_executor.py) that verifies the pre-expensive-call snapshot hook fires: set spent_usd > 0.10, invoke the executor step path, and assert a checkpoint was written before the model call. The evidence claims this is implemented (+42 lines in react_executor.py) but no test demonstrates the threshold gate works. Cite the test in the acceptance table.

The live demo in scripts/checkpoint_demo.py only verifies checkpoint files survive a simulated kill; it does not actually call resume_goal() and observe continued execution. Either (a) extend the demo to invoke resume_goal() with a fake LLM that produces a final answer, and show the resumed run completing, or (b) point to test_resume.py::test_kill_and_resume as the end-to-end proof and update the demo's printed output to clarify it only proves checkpoint durability, not resume execution.

Either implement these assertions against a real run_goal() with monkeypatched MAX_STEPS_THIS_RUN and call_model, or document in 'Out-of-spec changes' why the test was adapted and what the adaptation still proves.

Expose or document checkpoint_now(reason=...) per the brief's Architecture section ('Manually via checkpoint_now(reason="...") callable, used by the reviewer or by external callers'). It is not visible in agent/checkpoint.py per the diff. Add the callable and a test, or add it to 'Out-of-spec changes' with justification.
